candidates: When replacing a hardcoded large test string or fixture with a programmatic generator (e.g., `String.prototype.repeat`), verify that the generated output is exactly equivalent to the original character-for-character. A naive sub-pattern repetition can silently drop irregular sequences present in the original (e.g., consecutive identical tokens or an off-by-one tail), causing the test to exercise different behavior than intended. If exact reproduction requires a composite expression, use it; if the fixture must intentionally differ, update the assertion and document the change.

Tests that are intentionally not run in normal CI (e.g., because they take several minutes or require special infrastructure) must be written as `it.skip(...)` rather than left as an active test, and must include an inline comment explaining why the test is skipped.
